name: Signature

subjectOf.text: A signature under the Codex is defined functionally as the technical proof of the link between an identifier and a piece of digital information, not as a handwritten or format specific formality.
subjectOf.abstract: (1) The Signature is the technical proof between the Identifier and any Digital Information.
subjectOf.citation: Furrer Andreas, Wulf A. Kaal, Stephan D. Meyer, Universal Digital Law Codex (UDLC) (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5886342

subjectOf.text: Cryptographic attestation is evidentiary rather than dispositive of the continuity relation, so a valid signature does not by itself establish that the signing system is the registered subject.
subjectOf.abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939
